main_text.p: que accepta ? Ethicam profecto, quæ proba eft & genuina, à fcoriis omnibus humanæ nequitiæ per lympidam facrarum literarum laticem repurgata ? Ethicam quæ Hypocrifi ac Phantafticæ illi multorum pietati fitæ in compofitis gestibus, flexamina voce, fingulari vefti-mento, cæterifq; præftigiis, à qua generofa tua pietas maxime fuit femper aliena, larvam detrahit, oftenditq; non tantum optimam pietatem effe bonum animum, illud etiam alii dixere, fed omnem omnino probitatem ac Virtutem in animo confiftere ? Ethicam denique, quæ meo quidem arbitratu, digna eft, ut omnium manibus teratur, ac in ecclefia, & Academia anteponatur Ethicæ Ariftotelicæ, cæterifque, quæ per Scholas jam multos annos vagantur? in iis enim omnibus, quotquot mihi videre contigit, deeft Virtutis fundamentum, infuper confufum chaos funt, & præter nugas Scholafticas, terminos barbaros, inutiles Virtutum partitiones, otiofas quæftiones, de Virtute nihil, de ejus Officiis pauca reperiuntur: ut jam non dicam illos
Nota: the marks at the bottom left (H, ı, Π) are printer's signatures or stamps, not text.

page.notes: The scan is from a 16th–17th century Latin book. Some words in the transcription are uncertain because of the old type and print quality (for example "Ethicam" and "fingulari" at line ends). The page number is not printed on this page. The bottom-left marks are signature marks; the handwriting-like stains on the right edge are not transcribed.
